summary: 7 Wonders Duel reworks the drafting of its parent game into a tight two-player card-tableau battle, with cards laid out face-up and face-down in a pyramid so timing which card to grab (and which you deny your opponent) matters as much as what it does. Games can end abruptly via military or science victory well before the scoring phase, which makes it feel sharper and more confrontational than the original.
praised: excellent, tense two-player design with real head-to-head interaction
sudden-death military and science win conditions create real tension
fast to teach and play at around 30 minutes
criticised: military track can feel punishing if you fall behind early
less variance/variety than the multiplayer original for some tastes
first-player advantage debates in some editions/expansions

interaction.kind: drafting from a shared visible/hidden card display, a shared military track that can end the game outright, and a shared science track
interaction.detail: Both players draft from the same staggered card display, so timing and denial (taking a card your opponent needs, or unlocking one that helps only you) are central decisions every turn. The military track is a tug-of-war that can trigger sudden-death victory, and completing science sets can knock out an opponent's options, so the shared state is constantly being fought over rather than just built in parallel.
interaction.said: Commonly praised as far more interactive than the base game — reviewers say it 'ditches the solitaire feel', calling out the shared card row, direct military tug-of-war, and instant-win conditions as genuinely tense head-to-head play.

subsystems: civilian/economic card tableau (blue/yellow/purple cards, wonders, progress tokens, coins)
scoring.how_you_win: A player wins instantly by driving the conflict pawn into the opponent's capital (military) or collecting 6 different science symbols (science); if neither happens by the end of Age III, whoever has the higher total across all card/wonder/token/coin scoring wins.
scoring.score_note: military/science victories end game early, often below this range
